Memory of apps, services and containers is their cgroup's usage (shared memory counted once, file cache included); for single processes it is resident memory. disks.error: The folder could not be measured.

docker.title: Docker
docker.intro: Containers on this machine, through hearth-broker.
docker.state.no-broker.title: hearth-broker is not running
docker.state.no-broker.body: Hearth reaches Docker only through its helper, hearth-broker. Install the Hearth package (it sets up hearth-broker.socket) or start it with: sudo systemctl enable --now hearth-broker.socket
docker.state.not-member.title: You are not in the hearth group
docker.state.not-member.body: Only members of the hearth group may use hearth-broker. Add yourself with: sudo adduser $USER hearth — then log out and back in.
docker.state.no-docker.title: Docker is not available
docker.state.no-docker.body: Docker is not installed or not running. Install docker.io (or Docker Engine) and start docker.service.
docker.state.error.title: Docker could not be read
docker.none: No containers yet. Containers you create with docker run or docker compose appear here.
docker.problemBanner: {n} container(s) unhealthy or exited with an error.
docker.col.name: Container
docker.footnote: CPU is a share of one core (200% is two full cores); memory leaves out page cache, like docker stats. Usage is sampled every 2 s while this page is open.
docker.limit.title: Limits for {name}
docker.limit.intro: Applies at once while the container runs. Leave a field empty to keep what it has. Recreating the container, as Compose does, goes back to its own settings.
docker.authHint: If a password dialog appears, polkit is asking for permission to change Docker.
docker.confirmBody: This container and its writable layer are deleted. Named volumes are kept.
docker.confirmRunning: It is running: it will be stopped by force first.
detail.envMasked: Values of names containing PASSWORD, TOKEN, KEY or SECRET are hidden by hearth-broker; Hearth never receives them.
detail.risksBody: This container can reach the host beyond Docker's isolation:
detail.stats.none: No usage yet: the container is not running, or the first sample is on its way.
detail.logs.ended: The container stopped; no more output.
detail.logs.endedError: Log stream ended: {error}. Close and reopen the logs to follow them again.
detail.logs.foot: {n} line(s), newest at the bottom. Output is shown as plain text.
shell.intro: Opens /bin/sh inside the container. Your administrator password is asked every time.
shell.failed: No shell: {error}. Check that the container is running, then try again.
shell.refused: Hearth does not open a shell in this container: it can reach the host ({why}), so a shell in it would be a root shell on this machine.
reason.inUse: uses this image; it keeps running from it
docker.objects.name: Name
docker.objects.footNetworks: Docker's own bridge, host and none stay. A network with containers on it, stopped ones included, cannot be removed.
docker.objects.footVolumes: Sizes are measured when you open this tab. A volume with any container on it, stopped ones included, cannot be removed.
docker.objects.confirmNetwork: This network is deleted. No container uses it.
docker.objects.confirmVolume: Everything stored in this volume is deleted for good. It does not go to the trash.
image.total: {n} image(s), {size} in all (shared layers counted once per image)
image.none: No images yet. Images appear here once you pull or build one.
image.col.name: Image
image.footnote: Size counts every layer of the image; unique is what removing it alone would free (layers no other image uses).
image.pulling: Pulling {name}… this can take a while.
image.confirmBody: This image and all its tags are deleted; layers other images use are kept.
image.confirmInUse: Containers use this image. They keep running, but cannot be re-created from it until it is pulled again.
image.layersIntro: {n} history entries, newest first. Entries of 0 B only changed settings (CMD, ENV, LABEL…).
image.update.intro: Asks each tag's registry which image it serves now and compares it with the one pulled here. Nothing is downloaded.
image.update.untagged: An untagged image has nothing to compare.
image.update.local: built or tagged here: nothing to compare
image.scan.missing: Trivy is not installed. Install it (e.g. from aquasecurity's Debian repository) to scan images for known vulnerabilities.
image.scan.intro: Scans the image's packages with Trivy {version}. The first scan downloads Trivy's database and can take a few minutes.
image.scan.truncated: Only the 500 most severe are listed.
compose.none: No Compose projects. Containers started with docker compose appear here, grouped by project.
compose.reason.gone: the project has no containers any more
compose.footnote: Actions run on the project's existing containers, dependencies first when starting and last when stopping. Changing the compose file, creating or recreating containers is done with docker compose itself.
cleanup.containers.body: Containers that are created, exited or dead. Their writable layer goes; their images and named volumes stay.
cleanup.images.body: Dangling images: old layers left behind when a tag moved to a newer image. Tagged images are never touched here.
cleanup.networks.body: Networks no container is attached to (bridge, host and none are never removed).
cleanup.volumes.body: Volumes no container uses, not even a stopped one. They may hold data (databases, uploads) you still want.
cleanup.build.body: Cached build steps not in use. Builds get slower until the cache fills again.
cleanup.confirmBody: Exactly these are removed; anything created after this preview is left alone:
cleanup.volumesWarning: Volumes hold data. What is in them is deleted for good and cannot be recovered from Hearth.
cleanup.done: Removed {n}; {kept} kept because they are in use again.
cleanup.footnote: Sizes come from Docker and can overlap (a layer shared by two dangling images counts twice). Each removal asks for your password through polkit.

jobs.intro: Jobs that run on a schedule, as real systemd timers.
jobs.error: The jobs could not be read.
jobs.empty: No scheduled jobs yet. A job is a script that systemd runs on a schedule, as you or as root.
jobs.col.name: Job
jobs.rootHint: Runs as root; changing it asks for the administrator password.
jobs.confirmDeleteBody: Its timer, service and script are removed. A run in progress is stopped.

jobs.noRuns: No runs in the journal yet.

jobs.f.name: Name
jobs.f.everySpan: Every {span}, counted from the end of the last run.

jobs.f.scriptRoot: Runs as root from /var/lib/hearth/jobs, with no terminal. Anything it does is done with full privileges.
jobs.root.hint: Saving, running or changing a root job asks for the administrator password.
jobs.root.notMember: Root jobs need hearth-broker: add yourself to the hearth group (sudo adduser $USER hearth), then log out and back in.
jobs.root.noBroker: Root jobs need hearth-broker, which is not available.
jobs.root.authHint: The administrator password may be asked.

jobs.err.timeout: The time limit must be 1 minute to 7 days.

security.title: Security
security.intro: How exposed this computer is: open ports, the firewall, SSH, updates, automatic updates, known vulnerabilities, risky containers and programs others could replace. Hearth only looks; it changes nothing here.
security.verdict.warning: A few things deserve a look
security.unavailable: Could not check: {s}. Use Check again once that is fixed.
security.none.listeners: Every service listens only on this computer or on chosen addresses.
security.none.ssh: The SSH server's settings look safe.
security.none.cves: No known vulnerabilities affect the installed packages.
security.none.containers: No container can take over the host.
security.none.path: Only root and you can change the programs in PATH.
security.hint.listeners: A service on every address can be reached from the network. Bind it to 127.0.0.1 if only this computer uses it, or allow it in the firewall only from where it is needed.
security.hint.firewall: Turn on a firewall, for example: sudo apt install ufw && sudo ufw enable (incoming connections are then refused unless allowed).
security.hint.ssh: Edit a file in /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/ (PermitRootLogin no, PasswordAuthentication no once key logins work), then restart ssh.
security.hint.updates: Install the security updates from the Packages page.
security.hint.cves: Updates with a fix are listed on the Packages page; vulnerabilities without a fix need the package's maintainers.
security.hint.containers: These containers have access that equals root on this computer. Remove the option from their compose file unless they truly need it.
security.hint.path: Anyone who can write there can replace a program you run. Fix it with chmod o-w (or chown root:) on the path, or take the entry out of PATH.
security.hint.unattended: Hearth only reports this. To turn automatic security updates on, run: sudo dpkg-reconfigure unattended-upgrades
security.f.unattended_never: On, but it has not run yet
security.f.unattended_stale: On, but it last ran on {s}
security.f.unattended_off: unattended-upgrades is installed but turned off
security.f.unattended_no_lists: Package lists are not refreshed automatically, so no new updates are found
security.f.unattended_no_timer: {s} is not active, so it does not run
security.f.unattended_no_tool: unattended-upgrades is not installed: updates wait for you
security.hint.restart: After an update, old code keeps running until what uses it restarts.
security.f.restart_reboot: This machine asks for a restart
security.f.restart_no_tool: Install needrestart to see which services still run old libraries
security.f.restart_scan_failed: The check for old libraries failed
home.restart.reboot: A restart is waiting: an update needs it to take effect.

security.f.app_danger: The app {s} runs with danger flags
security.f.app_exposed: The app {s} is reachable from the network

profiles.app.hint: Apps are only started. A profile never closes an app, because that could lose unsaved work.
profiles.confirmBody: This will change now. Deactivating the profile puts it back.
profiles.confirmDeleteBody: Only the profile is deleted; nothing on the system changes.

insight.title: Heat and energy
insight.intro: Why this computer is warm or loud right now, and roughly what uses its energy.

insight.cause.quiet: Nothing is making much heat right now. If the fan is loud anyway, that is the firmware's choice, or the vents need cleaning.

integrity.title: Integrity watch
integrity.intro: Watches your SSH access, shell start files, autostart entries, your own services and ~/.local/bin, and tells you when one changes. It only reads, as your user.
integrity.error: Could not read the integrity watch.
integrity.failed: The scan failed. Reload the page to scan again; if it fails again, Hearth's log has the cause: journalctl --user -u hearthd.
integrity.since: Baseline from {time}, {n} items. Whatever was there then was trusted as it was.
integrity.clean: Nothing has changed since the baseline.
integrity.more: {n} more are not listed. Accept these to see them.
integrity.truncated: There are too many files to watch them all, so some are not covered and removed files are not reported.
integrity.confirmBody: Only accept changes you recognize. The watch will treat these as normal from now on:
integrity.moved: A file changed again, so it was not accepted. Check it again.
integrity.diffCut: The rest of this comparison is not shown.
integrity.note.notext: This cannot be shown as text: it is binary, large, unreadable or only a name.
integrity.note.hidden: Only lines that may hold a secret changed. They stay hidden, so check this file yourself.
integrity.systemIntro: Names only. Hearth does not open these files, so a change inside one is not noticed.
integrity.unreadable: Your user cannot list this folder.
access.title: Access
access.intro: Who can get in and who has: SSH logins from the journal, sessions open now and the accounts on this computer. It only reads.
access.limited: The system journal is out of this user's reach, so SSH logins cannot be shown. Adding the user to the systemd-journal group gives access.
access.noLogins: No SSH logins or failed attempts in the journal.
access.cut: Only the newest entries were counted.
access.sessionsError: Could not ask logind for sessions. Check that systemd-logind is running, then reload the page.
access.usersError: Could not read the user list in /etc/passwd and /etc/group. Check that both are readable, then reload the page.
access.usersNote: Lists root, regular accounts and anyone in sudo or docker. Members of the docker group can control the host as root.
tokens.title: Tokens
tokens.intro: Read-only tokens let the hearth command and a metrics scraper on this computer see a few read-only lists. A token cannot change anything, open a terminal or read logs.
tokens.name: Name
tokens.nameHint: A name is 1 to 32 lowercase letters, digits or hyphens. Each token is saved in the file shown, which only you can read; Hearth never shows it here.
tokens.revokeBody: It stops working at once and its file is deleted. Anything using it will be refused until it has a new one.
tokens.cliNeeds: The hearth command reads the token named cli. Create it above, then run:
tokens.cliReady: The hearth command uses the token named cli. In a terminal:
tokens.metricsIntro: An OpenMetrics page at /metrics on this computer's loopback address only, for a local Prometheus. It needs a read-only token.
tokens.metricsHow: A Prometheus job for it, reading the token from its file:
compose.updateBody: Pulls each service's image and recreates what changed. Containers restart, and only what is in volumes or bind mounts is kept. Images that need a registry login cannot be pulled. Variables from your shell are not used; a .env file in the project folder is.
compose.updateHint: Your password is needed. This can take minutes while images download.
docker.composeMoved: Compose projects are on the Apps page
stacks.title: Apps
stacks.intro: Apps Hearth manages, and the Compose projects it only detects.
stacks.detectedIntro: These keep working as they are. Importing is optional and starts with a dry-run that changes nothing.
stacks.error: The apps could not be read.
stacks.none: No app is managed yet. Check a detected project to import it.
stacks.updateBody: Pulls exactly the image versions listed, then recreates the containers that change. Data stays.
stacks.removeBody: Removes the app's containers and Hearth's files for it. Its volumes and folders stay.
stacks.removeVolumesBody: Removes the app's containers, its files, and deletes its volumes and their data. Folders on this computer stay.
stacks.importError: The dry-run could not be made.
stacks.secretsMoved: {n} values move into the app's secrets file. They are not shown.
stacks.importBlocked: {name} cannot be imported yet: see what is refused.
